principle: Each stroke family is analyzed as a sequence of coaching questions. Metrics are evidence for questions, not the product itself.

questions: Did the player buy enough time with recognition and preparation for this incoming ball?
Did the feet create a viable strike distance for the chosen stance and direction?
Was load/balance appropriate to the ball and intended shot rather than merely visually conventional?
Did pelvis/trunk/arm/racket contributions organize the swing without an obvious rescue compensation?
Was contact geometry compatible with the intended trajectory?
Did the racket path produce the intended launch/spin proxy without excessive late correction?
Did recovery begin in time for the next likely ball?

questions: Was side recognition and shoulder organization early enough?
Did the last adjustment steps preserve hitting radius instead of crowding the torso?
Did trunk and both arms work as the player's repeatable technique family rather than separating under pressure?
Does the racket path change because of an upstream spacing/timing issue?
Which self-best reps solve the same ball with less compensation?
